topic: The Magic of Quantum Superposition: Bridging Classical and Quantum Realities

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
lecture_lines: Classical systems exist in one definite state.
A light switch is either ON or OFF.
There is no middle ground in classical physics.
animations: Create a classic ball with label "Classic" in #FFFFFF.
Create a quantum cloud with label "Quantum" in #FF00FF.
Transition "Classic" to movement along a discrete path.
Highlight divergence of both paths with #FFFF00.

sections.title: Visualizing Superposition: The Mathematical Foundation
lecture_lines: Quantum superposition allows multiple states simultaneously.
Dirac notation describes this mathematical state.
The Bloch Sphere visualizes these probabilities.
Think of a spinning coin's blur.
It exists as both heads and tails.
animations: Display state vector |0> as a vector in #00FFFF.
Display state vector |1> as a vector in #FFFF00.
Overlay complex coefficients a and b in #FFFFFF.
Animate linear combination a|0> + b|1> in #FF00FF.
Show state vector rotating in the Bloch sphere.

sections.title: The Wave-Particle Duality
lecture_lines: Superposition is interference between these waves.
animations: Display a localized point particle in #FFFFFF.
Display a spread-out wave packet in #00FFFF.
Animate the point vs wave transition in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Act of Measurement: Wave Function Collapse
lecture_lines: Observation forces the wave function to collapse.
The system chooses one definite state.
Schrödinger's cat illustrates this measurement paradox.
The box reveal forces reality to resolve.
animations: Show wave function ψ across a space.
Display an observer icon in #FFFF00 appearing.
Animate sudden collapse of ψ to a single peak.

sections.title: Quantum Advantage: Why Superposition Matters
lecture_lines: Superposition powers quantum computing's parallel advantage.
Classical bits process sequentially, quantum bits parallel.
Quantum computers solve complex problems instantly.
animations: Show parallel paths for a classical bit.
Show branching superposition for a qubit.
